microtheory.name: modal_logic
microtheory.definition: Logic of necessity + possibility. Kripke semantics, accessibility relations, modal systems (K, T, S4, S5), temporal logic, epistemic logic, deontic logic, doxastic logic. Substrate analogue: substrate's reasoning about possibility + necessity across Mt-states.

concepts.name: modal_operator
concepts.definition: □ (necessarily), ◇ (possibly). Box + diamond. Substrate analogue: substrate's modal-status concept.

concepts.name: necessity
concepts.definition: True in all possible worlds. □P. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-invariant truth.

concepts.name: possibility
concepts.definition: True in some possible world. ◇P. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-satisfiable truth.

concepts.name: modal_duality
concepts.definition: □P ≡ ¬◇¬P. Necessity is impossibility of contrary. Substrate analogue: substrate's modal-conversion.

concepts.name: kripke_semantics
concepts.definition: Kripke 1959. Models = (W, R, V). Worlds + accessibility relation + valuation. □P true at w iff P true at all w' accessible from w. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-network semantics.

concepts.name: possible_world
concepts.definition: Way the world could be. Modal logic primitive. Substrate analogue: substrate's possible Mt-state.

concepts.name: accessibility_relation
concepts.definition: R between worlds. wRw' = w' is possible-relative-to w. Different modal systems by R's properties. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-reachability.

concepts.name: model_modal
concepts.definition: Kripke model. (W, R, V) where V assigns truth-values per world. Substrate analogue: substrate's branching state-graph.

concepts.name: modal_system_k
concepts.definition: Weakest normal modal logic. Only axiom: □(P→Q) → (□P → □Q). Substrate analogue: substrate's minimal modal reasoning.

concepts.name: modal_system_t
concepts.definition: K + (□P → P). Reflexive R: everything actual is possible. Substrate analogue: substrate's grounded modality.

concepts.name: modal_system_s4
concepts.definition: T + (□P → □□P). Transitive R: necessities are necessarily necessary. Substrate analogue: substrate's stable modality.

concepts.name: modal_system_s5
concepts.definition: T + (◇P → □◇P). R is equivalence relation. Strongest standard. Substrate analogue: substrate's collapsed modality.

concepts.name: rigid_designator_modal
concepts.definition: Kripke. Term referring to same thing in all possible worlds. Names are rigid. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-Concept across basins.

concepts.name: transworld_identity
concepts.definition: Same individual across possible worlds. Counterpart theory (Lewis) denies strict identity. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-identity across states.

concepts.name: essentialism
concepts.definition: Some properties necessary to objects. Water is necessarily H2O. Substrate analogue: substrate's required-Concept properties.

concepts.name: temporal_logic
concepts.definition: Modal with temporal operators. F (future), P (past), G (always), H (always was). Prior. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-relation reasoning.

concepts.name: ltl
concepts.definition: Linear Temporal Logic. Time as linear sequence. Used in verification. Substrate analogue: substrate's sequential-state reasoning.

concepts.name: ctl
concepts.definition: Computation Tree Logic. Time as branching. Substrate analogue: substrate's branching-future reasoning.

concepts.name: epistemic_logic
concepts.definition: Modal with knowledge operator K. KP = agent knows P. Hintikka 1962. Substrate analogue: substrate's knowledge reasoning.

concepts.name: knowledge_axioms
concepts.definition: Axiom T: KP → P (knowledge is factive). Axiom 4: KP → KKP (positive introspection). Axiom 5: ¬KP → K¬KP (negative introspection). Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective principles.

concepts.name: common_knowledge_logic
concepts.definition: Everyone knows everyone knows ... arbitrary depth. Coordination problems require it. Substrate analogue: substrate's shared-common-ground.

concepts.name: muddy_children_puzzle
concepts.definition: Classic common knowledge puzzle. After n announcements, the n muddy children know they're muddy. Substrate analogue: substrate's iterated reasoning.

concepts.name: deontic_logic
concepts.definition: Modal with obligation O + permission P. Reasoning about norms. Substrate analogue: substrate's normative reasoning.

concepts.name: obligation
concepts.definition: Must do. OP. Substrate analogue: substrate's required-action.

concepts.name: permission_deontic
concepts.definition: May do. PP. Substrate analogue: substrate's allowed-action.

concepts.name: deontic_paradoxes
concepts.definition: Ross's paradox, Chisholm's paradox, etc. Difficulties of formalizing norms. Substrate analogue: substrate's normative-inference problems.

concepts.name: doxastic_logic
concepts.definition: Modal with belief operator B. BP = agent believes P. Weaker than K. Substrate analogue: substrate's belief reasoning.

concepts.name: belief_versus_knowledge
concepts.definition: Knowledge requires truth; belief doesn't. KP → BP, not vice versa. Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-vs-truth distinction.

concepts.name: dynamic_logic
concepts.definition: Modal with program operators [α]. After executing α, P. Hoare logic style. Substrate analogue: substrate's action-effect reasoning.

concepts.name: modal_logic_program_verification
concepts.definition: Use modal logics to specify + verify programs. Pnueli. Substrate analogue: substrate's behavior-verification.

rules.name: necessity_distributes_over_implication
rules.head: the substrate accepts □(P→Q) and □P
rules.body: it can conclude □Q. Modal modus ponens. Axiom K.

rules.name: reflexive_accessibility_grounds_actuality
rules.head: the substrate uses reflexive accessibility relation
rules.body: every necessary truth is actually true. □P → P. System T.

rules.name: knowledge_implies_truth
rules.head: the substrate KNOWS that P
rules.body: P must be true. Knowledge is factive. Hintikka. Substrate's K-T axiom.

rules.name: rigid_designation_supports_modal_identity
rules.head: the substrate uses a rigid designator
rules.body: the term picks out the same entity in every possible world. Kripke. Substrate's persistent Concept across basins.

rules.name: temporal_logic_handles_time_reasoning
rules.head: the substrate reasons about temporal sequences
rules.body: temporal modal operators (F, P, G, H) provide the language. LTL or CTL by structure.
